youtube_title: How Hitchcock paid for Psycho himself (1960) #shorts
tiktok_caption:
Paramount would not pay for Psycho, so Hitchcock paid for it himself and kept sixty percent of the film 🎬 It cost about eight hundred thousand dollars and he later said it had made fifteen million. It also earned him his fifth and final Oscar nomination for best director. He lost that one too.

instagram_caption:
Alfred Hitchcock had to fund Psycho himself 🎬

In 1959 Paramount balked at his plans for the film. So he made an offer: he would skip his quarter-million-dollar fee and bankroll it, in return for sixty percent of the picture. He shot it in black and white with his television crew on the Universal lot for about eight hundred thousand dollars.

The shower scene took seven days, more than seventy shots for forty-five seconds of screen time, with chocolate syrup for blood. Then came the rule: nobody admitted after the film started, enforced by a life-size cardboard Hitchcock pointing at his watch.

By his own count the film had made fifteen million dollars by 1966, and trade papers put his share at five or six million. Fun fact: he had bought the rights to the novel anonymously for about nine thousand dollars.

Psycho also brought him an Oscar nomination for best director. His fifth. He lost, as he had the other four times. In 1968 the Academy gave him an honorary award instead. His entire speech: Thank you.
